points.description: Defines the bandwidth-delay product as the link capacity (bandwidth) multiplied by the one-way propagation delay.
States that it represents the amount of data that can be in flight on the link at one time.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both the definition as capacity times one-way propagation delay and the interpretation as the amount of data in flight on the link. Each idea is worth one mark and is all or nothing. A definition that only gives the formula without the meaning, or only the meaning without the formula, earns one mark.
